headline: Southborough secured a $3.9 million culvert grant, approved an architect for the Neary school project, and adjusted multiple capital funding plans.
synopsis: Southborough was awarded nearly $3.9 million in state culvert grants, allowing the town to avoid taking on debt previously authorized by Town Meeting. The Select Board approved a feasibility study contract with Tappe Architects for the Neary Elementary School project and awarded a repair bid for the Town Common fence, while the School Committee appointed Daniel Mazur as director of student support services. Regulatory boards addressed major development proposals, including a 32-unit Chapter 40B project on Turnpike Road and occupancy conditions for 200 Turnpike Road. Meanwhile, the Trails and Golf committees confronted rising costs and revised their Community Preservation Act funding strategies.

highlights.title: Town awarded $3.9 million state culvert grant
highlights.why: The grant covers infrastructure replacements across town, enabling Southborough to avoid issuing $3.9 million in borrowing that Town Meeting had previously approved.

highlights.title: Neary school feasibility study contract approved
highlights.why: The Select Board approved a contract with Tappe Architects requiring objective evaluations and preliminary designs for both Town Meeting school options.

highlights.title: Conservation review of 32-unit Turnpike Road housing project
highlights.why: The commission reviewed buffer zone alterations and wildlife crossings for a proposed Chapter 40B development at 250 Turnpike Road before continuing the hearing to June 25.

highlights.title: Trails Committee scales back CPA request to bridge only
highlights.why: With combined bridge and boardwalk estimates reaching $630,000, the committee decided to seek Community Preservation Act funds only for the $410,000 bridge portion.

highlights.title: Daniel Mazur appointed director of student support services
highlights.why: The School Committee voted unanimously to hire Mazur to lead K-8 student support services, targeting a July 1 start date.

highlights.title: Town Common fence restoration contract awarded
highlights.why: The Select Board awarded a $70,500 base bid to Kneeland Construction to restore and repair the existing Town Common fence using Community Preservation Act funds.
